hints: An optimal school serves a consecutive interval of houses.
The best school position for one interval is a weighted median of its children.
Use interval-cost DP with divide-and-conquer optimization of monotone best split points.
analogy: A school placed at the weighted middle balances the walking distance of children on either side.
example: For child counts [1,1,1] and one school, place it at house 2 for total distance 2.
algorithm: Precompute interval costs cost(l,r) using weighted medians and prefix sums of child counts and weighted positions. Let dp[g][i] be the minimum cost to serve the first i houses with g schools; transition over j<i using dp[g-1][j]+cost(j+1,i). Compute each DP layer by divide-and-conquer optimization, searching monotone ranges of optimal split indices. Use wide integers.
correctness: One-dimensional nearest-school assignments form consecutive intervals, and their optimal single school is a weighted median. The recurrence covers every partition; its interval costs have the Monge property, giving nondecreasing optimal split points and validating the restricted searches.
complexity: For n houses and k schools, O(n^2+kn log n) time and O(n^2+n) space after precomputing interval costs.
